scenario_summary: Customer is requesting a refund for a service canceled 34 days ago, which falls just outside the standard 30-day refund window.

conversation.message: Hi, my name is Carlos Rodriguez and I'm 27. I'm trying to get a refund for a service I canceled 34 days ago. I know your refund policy is usually 30 days, but I was traveling and only just saw the charge — I didn't realize it had gone through until now. Is there anything you can do?

Hello Carlos, thanks for reaching out. I understand you're looking for a refund outside of our standard window. To look into this for you, could you please provide the email address associated with your account and the transaction ID for the charge?
Sure, the email is carlos.rod@email.com and the transaction ID is TXN-99821-B.
Thanks for that. Just to confirm, can you verify your full billing address on file so I can pull up the account details?

Thank you. I see the charge here from 34 days ago. Per our standard Terms of Service, specifically the Refund Eligibility section, we only process refunds within 30 days of the transaction date. Since you are outside that window, I'm not authorized to process this directly.
I understand the policy, but given the circumstances of my travel, is there really no flexibility? It's only 4 days over.

I hear you, and I know it's frustrating. Because I don't have the system permissions to override the 30-day limit, I'm going to escalate this to our billing specialist team. They have the authority to review exceptions for cases like yours.
Okay, I appreciate you trying. How long will that take?
I've submitted the request to the specialist queue now. You should receive an update via email within 2-3 business days. Is there anything else I can help you with today?

escalation_reason: Agent lacked the system permissions to override the 30-day refund policy window and referred the case to the billing specialist team for exception review.

judge_scores.justification: The agent conducted appropriate verification, clearly cited the 30-day Terms of Service refund policy, and efficiently gathered necessary account details without redundancy. While resolution effort was limited by authority constraints regarding the 30-day window, the escalation to the billing specialist team was entirely appropriate for handling a policy exception.
